# zstd / huf_round_trip

zstd's own fuzz target `huf_round_trip` ([source](source/huf_round_trip.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over zstd (facebook/zstd at 82d322c4).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: Histogram, build and write a Huffman CTable, read it back as a DTable (X1, or X2 falling back to X1), HUF_compress1X/4X then decompress: if compression produced output, decompression must succeed, regenerate the size and match. RLE and incompressible inputs (cSize == 0, or table write failure) are skipped.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against zstd at commit 82d322c4.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- HIST_count, HUF_buildCTable_wksp and HUF_readDTable must succeed, HUF_optimalTableLog must return <= 12, maxSymbol <= 255 ([lines 71-109](source/huf_round_trip.c#L71-L109)): abort(); confirmed in the binary.
- Histogram, build and write a Huffman CTable, read it back as a DTable (X1, or X2 falling back to X1), HUF_compress1X/4X then decompress: if compression produced output, decompression must succeed, regenerate the size and match. RLE and incompressible inputs (cSize == 0, or table write failure) are skipped ([lines 111-128](source/huf_round_trip.c#L111-L128)): abort(); confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies them on every input it covers.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch zstd` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `huf_round_trip.plain` | 111,656 | `1347a25a5b3a82aca6b94b4489ee5d7ae4f1ca80b7f0b061b4d6b01ac9012e6a` |

| asan | `huf_round_trip.asan` | 723,464 | `54d9146bd04ff7a9a5fb264bdfea3fab82aeb2bc4ea5164b6fef2ca504293cb8` |
| asan-ubsan | `huf_round_trip.asan-ubsan` | 747,800 | `21c442f2eb8777c979215d856c832812f42db8fe429afbdb426344e7becd2ec8` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
